content.user_title: Diagnose and Prioritize Enterprise Data Assets
content.value_statement: Organizations often lack a reliable view of which data resources deserve investment. This skill maps, scores, and prioritizes assets for focused next steps.
actual_capabilities: Maps data resources by source, form, scale, quality, and business scenario.
Structures stakeholder discovery with a three-stage, nine-question interview method.
Scores resources across scarcity, quality, ownership, use cases, and compliance risk.
Places resources into priority, challenge, reserve, or stop quadrants.
Designs inventory plans, interview guides, checklists, diagnostic reports, and executive briefings.
Identifies inflated volume claims and recommends sampling and metadata checks.
limitations: Results depend on complete, accurate stakeholder answers and supporting evidence.
The skill does not directly connect to systems or validate databases.
Its diagnosis does not replace formal valuation, quality certification, or legal advice.
The source guidance is in Chinese and references Chinese standards and policies.

use_cases.title: Plan an Initial Data Inventory
use_cases.description: Create a focused inventory scope, evidence request, interview plan, and delivery schedule.

use_cases.title: Select First Data Asset Projects
use_cases.description: Score candidate resources and select one to three practical projects for the first phase.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Executive Diagnosis
use_cases.description: Turn inventory evidence into a heat map, priority matrix, risk list, and action plan.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a data inventory plan for [organization]. Cover [scope] and list the documents, stakeholders, and nine interview questions required.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new inventory

prompt_templates.title: Score Candidate Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Score these data resources using the DMS weights: [resources and evidence]. Show each factor, assumption, total score, and recommended category.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Data Volume Claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this data volume claim: [claim]. Design read-only sampling, screenshot, metadata, and database-statistic checks without retaining source data.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Executive Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [inventory evidence] to create a full diagnosis. Include quality and ownership risks, a priority matrix, three first projects, costs, benefits, and dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced portfolio diagnosis and decision support

output_examples.input: Score customer service records with strong demand, moderate quality, clear ownership, and low compliance risk.
output: Main strength: Clear business demand and ownership.
Main gap: Improve quality controls before expansion.
Next step: Define a limited pilot with measurable outcomes.

output_examples.input: Design a two-week inventory for one business unit with five systems and limited documentation.
output: Days 1-2: Confirm scope, owners, confidentiality, and evidence requests.
Days 3-6: Interview business, IT, data, and finance stakeholders.
Days 7-9: Verify metadata, volumes, quality indicators, ownership, and risks.
Day 10: Present the resource map, scores, priorities, and next actions.

best_practices: Require evidence for every score, assumption, and recommendation.
Keep only necessary metadata and avoid retaining source data.
Start with one to three feasible projects before expanding the portfolio.
anti_patterns: Do not accept reported data volumes without independent checks.
Do not treat an initial diagnosis as a legal opinion or formal valuation.
Do not prioritize value before resolving ownership and compliance concerns.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the business scope, system list, data dictionary, process documents, candidate resources, known risks, and available evidence.

faq.question: Does the skill access enterprise systems?
faq.answer: No. It provides methods and deliverables based on supplied information and recommends read-only validation.

faq.question: How does the scoring model work?
faq.answer: It weights scale and scarcity, quality, ownership, scenarios, and compliance risk to produce a score out of 100.

faq.question: How many projects should start first?
faq.answer: The method recommends one to three high-value, feasible projects for the first phase.

faq.question: Can the result replace legal or valuation advice?
faq.answer: No. Ownership, compliance, accounting, and valuation conclusions require qualified professional review.

faq.question: Which standards does the guidance reference?
faq.answer: It references Chinese data management, quality, classification, accounting, and valuation guidance described in the bundled knowledge base.
